subject: math
title: JC H2 functions and graphs: transformations, reciprocal functions, asymptote behaviour

questions.prompt: The graph of y = f(x) has a root at x = 0. Where is the corresponding root of y = f(x + 3)?

choices.text: At x = 3, three units to the right
At x = -3, three units to the left

questions.misconception: f(x + 3) shifts the graph 3 units to the right.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: f(x + 3) shifts the graph 3 units to the right. In fact f(x + 3) is zero when x + 3 = 0, that is at x = -3, so the graph shifts 3 units to the LEFT: a change inside the brackets moves the graph in the opposite direction to the sign.

questions.prompt: Which equation is y = f(x) stretched vertically by a factor of 3 and then lifted up by 2?
questions.explanation: Both changes act outside f, so both act vertically: multiplying by 3 stretches every height by a factor of 3, and adding 2 at the end lifts the graph by 2. The choice f(3x) squeezes horizontally instead, because the 3 is inside the brackets.

questions.prompt: Rewrite f(2x + 6) in the form f(2(x + c)) and state the horizontal translation it shows.
questions.answer: f(2x + 6) = f(2(x + 3)): a translation of 3 units to the left, then a horizontal squeeze by a factor of 2.
questions.explanation: Factor out the 2 before reading the shift: 2x + 6 = 2(x + 3), so the inside change is x + 3, which shifts the graph left by 3 - reading the 6 directly would give the wrong shift.

questions.prompt: State the equations of the vertical and horizontal asymptotes of y = 1/(x - 2) + 1.
questions.answer: Vertical asymptote x = 2; horizontal asymptote y = 1.
questions.explanation: The denominator is zero at x = 2, so the curve shoots up the line x = 2 and never touches it. As x grows large, 1/(x - 2) shrinks toward 0, so the curve flattens onto y = 0 + 1 = 1.

questions.prompt: As x approaches 0 from the positive side, what does the graph of y = 1/x do?

choices.text: It flattens onto the line y = 0
It shoots up without bound along the line x = 0
It crosses the line x = 0 at a high point

questions.explanation: Close to x = 0 the values of 1/x grow without bound, so the branch hugs the vertical asymptote x = 0 and never crosses it. Flattening onto y = 0 is what happens as x grows large, at the horizontal asymptote.
